terms.gloss: sup up, suck in, drink down (soup, an egg); slurp
evidence: Plaut. Most. 791: simul flāre sorbēreque haud factū facilest
terms.comment: The proverb is Plautus’s: you can’t blow and sup at the same time.

phrases.latin: Avia herbārum īnfūsum ē pōcillō paulātim sorbillābat
phrases.english: Grandma was slowly sipping herbal tea from her cup

phrases.latin: Sorbet dormiēns. — Quid, sorbet? — Illud, stertit, voluī dīcere.
phrases.english: He’s slurping in his sleep. — What, slurping? — Snoring, I meant to say.

sources: Lewis & Short: sorbillo · Lewis & Short: sorbeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 73.
